text:
Amira: quick sync — debating our DEK cache strategy for cross-cloud private deployments. specific constraints: multi-kms (aws/gcp/az) + requirement that unwraps are auditable per-tenant. thinking: short-lived DEK cache, binding to instance identity, and forced re-unwrap on RBAC change. thoughts?

Tariq: +1 on binding to instance. implementation idea: store cached DEK encrypted with local node key (not KEK) + HMAC of instance id & PID. cache TTL = 5m default, with jitter. unwrap -> fetch DEK from KMS only on miss or ttl expiry. this reduces KMS QPS while keeping exposure window small.

Mel: what about audit logs? we need a way to correlate unwrap ops with tenant IDs and the reason (initial load vs rbca change vs rotation). KMS audit logs are messy across clouds. propose we emit structured events to our audit pipeline on every unwrap/rotate (signed by the node) containing: tenant_id, key_id, op_reason, node_cert_fingerprint.

Jonathan: incident scenario: if KMS global outage in region, cached DEKs let apps keep serving but we also risk stale permissions if RBAC changes. can we gate cached DEKs with a revocation check? e.g., short cache + a revocation list push from control plane. if revocation present, node invalidates immediately.

Amira: revocation list push makes sense. scale concern: if large fleet, pushes could be noisy. TTL + delta push of changed tenants only? also need to avoid DOS from large revocation storms.

Tariq: agree — implement delta-sync + rate-limit on revocation application. also add backoff when KMS is flapping so we don't exhaust keys on repeated unwraps. sample pseudoconfig: 
```
envelope_cache:
  mode: per_node
  cache_ttl_ms: 300000
  jitter_ms: 60000
  max_unwrap_retries: 3
  revocation_poll_interval_ms: 60000
  revocation_push_batch_size: 100
  bind_to: [instance_id, node_cert_fingerprint]
```

Mel: RBAC changes: we need a safe rollout path. when owner removes a tenant's access, control plane should enqueue revocation and emit audit_event("revocation_scheduled", ...). on nodes: receive delta -> invalidate any cached DEKs for matching tenant -> emit audit_event("cached_dek_invalidated", ...). that gives an auditable chain.

Jonathan: one more: DEK/KEK separation — KEK stays in KMS, DEK ephemeral. but for cross-cloud, evaluate using KMS-as-KEK + local HSM for ephemeral node key. or use customer-managed KEK in each cloud and an abstraction layer. must document threat model: if node key compromised, attacker can unwrap cached DEKs while within TTL. minimize blast radius by: short ttl, per-tenant DEKs (not global), and key usage tags.

Amira: vuln triage: if we detect node compromise (via suspicious process), oncall should trigger mass revocation for that node's certificate and issue tenant revocations for any DEKs issued to that node in the last X minutes. how to query nodes for active cached keys quickly? we have a /node-status endpoint that returns a digest of cached dek metadata (sha256 list) — not secret. on revocation, control plane sends matching sha256 to nodes to invalidate.

sec-bot: incident-runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kms-cache-compromise. recommended TLDR: 1) revoke node cert, 2) push tenant revocations, 3) rotate KEKs if scope unknown, 4) require re-wrap via KMS once healthy. :warning:

Mel: logging requirement: every unwrap must produce two records: one local structured log (node, tenant, key_id, reason, hmac) and one central audit_event with the same correlation_id. correlate by correlation_id in SIEM. retention policy: unwrap events kept 2 years.

Tariq: perf note: we should sample unwraps for full payload logging (don't log DEK material). just record metadata and a short, hashed audit blob. code snippet for envelope header: 
```
{
  "version": 1,
  "tenant_id": "t-123",
  "key_id": "aws:kms:arn:...",
  "wrapped_dek": "...",
  "node_binding": "hmac(instance_id, node_cert_fingerprint)",
  "audit_nonce": "uuid4()"
}
```

Jonathan: ops question — how many KMS calls per 1k requests with caching? with ttl=5m and avg session requests ~200/s per node you'll get <1 unwrap/s per tenant per node. recommend we simulate with our workload generator and tune ttl per-workload.

Amira: action items: Tariq to prototype cache binding + delta revocation; Mel to draft audit schema & retention; Jonathan to simulate KMS QPS for 3 typical workloads; I'll update runbook with revocation push steps. thanks all. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Reminder: escalations for potential key compromise are in the runbook. If you trigger a revocation, ping #oncall immediately.
